title: Withdrawal of the First Generation Entertainment Head End Server
abstract: Replacement of the original entertainment head end server by an interim unit of the same generation, issued when the original storage technology could no longer be repaired and the fleet had no supportable server.

sections.reason: The rotating storage array in the original head end server reached the end of its supportable life in 2018, with no repair source and no qualified drop-in replacement drive. Server-attributed cabin defects had risen to 4.8 per thousand flight hours and the mean time between unscheduled removals had fallen to 2 100 hours against a design figure of 9 000. Operators were carrying spare servers as line stock, which for a unit of this size and price was not sustainable.
sections.description: The server is replaced by an interim unit built on solid state storage in the same chassis envelope, using the existing partition D4420121334529 and the upper partition D4420125490996 in the equipment rack without change. The obsolete seat track cover D4420127529323 at the rack front is deleted and the aperture is closed by the revised stowage bin item D4420129816843. Anchor nuts EN258434K3 secure the revised rack front. The unit runs boot software LC5R2884353 and parameter set LC4RABC2783, both re-issued for the new storage controller. The galley insert at FIN 7RK6 is disturbed for access and refitted unchanged. Installation is in zones 916 and 941. No change is made to the seat display units or to their distribution.
sections.effects: Mass reduction of 14 kg per aircraft. Electrical load falls by 260 VA on the entertainment busbar, and the heat rejected into the rack falls with it, which removes the rack ventilation restriction previously placed on hot-station turnrounds. The interim unit is not interchangeable with the original because the software standards differ. Despatch with the entertainment system inoperative was already available and is unchanged. Illustrated parts content for the rack front requires update.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only, through a service bulletin, as an overnight line task of about seven hours. The standard is offered to every operator still at the original server standard and is expected to remain the fleet standard for the supportable life of the chassis.

type_data.production_impact: No production cut-in; affected aircraft had already left the line

title: Withdrawal of the First Generation Entertainment Head End Server

issue.reason: Supersession by the second generation architecture declared, with a conversion matrix stating what is removed and what is carried over from each standard.

abstract: Replacement of the original entertainment head end server by an interim unit of the same generation, issued when the original storage technology could no longer be repaired and before the second generation architecture was available.

sections.reason: The rotating storage array in the original head end server reached the end of its supportable life in 2018, with no repair source and no qualified drop-in replacement drive. Server-attributed cabin defects had risen to 4.8 per thousand flight hours and the mean time between unscheduled removals had fallen to 2 100 hours against a design figure of 9 000. Operators were carrying spare servers as line stock, which for a unit of this size and price was not sustainable.
sections.description: The server is replaced by an interim unit built on solid state storage in the same chassis envelope, using the existing partition D4420121334529 and the upper partition D4420125490996 in the equipment rack without change. The obsolete seat track cover D4420127529323 at the rack front is deleted and the aperture is closed by the revised stowage bin item D4420129816843. Anchor nuts EN258434K3 secure the revised rack front. The unit runs boot software LC5R2884353 and parameter set LC4RABC2783, both re-issued for the new storage controller. The galley insert at FIN 7RK6 is disturbed for access and refitted unchanged. Installation is in zones 916 and 941. No change is made to the seat display units or to their distribution.
sections.effects: Mass reduction of 14 kg per aircraft. Electrical load falls by 260 VA on the entertainment busbar, and the heat rejected into the rack falls with it, which removes the rack ventilation restriction previously placed on hot-station turnrounds. The interim unit is not interchangeable with the original because the software standards differ, and it is not interchangeable forward either: the second generation unit does not mate with the backplane loom installed here. Despatch with the entertainment system inoperative was already available and is unchanged. Illustrated parts content for the rack front requires update.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only, through a service bulletin, as an overnight line task of about seven hours. This standard was always intended as a bridge and it is superseded by the second generation architecture, which takes the same rack position with a different backplane and a different cooling path; no aircraft can carry both. A conversion matrix is issued with this issue and states, per starting standard, what is removed and what is carried over: from the original standard the partitions and the rack front stay and the server, its cabling loom and its software are replaced; from this interim standard the partitions and the revised rack front stay, the stowage bin item is re-used, and the unit, the backplane loom and both loadable standards are replaced. Aircraft that have not yet embodied this standard are to go directly to the second generation.

type_data.production_impact: No production cut-in; affected aircraft had already left the line
